Description: Insecure handling of the Proxy-Authorization header in FastAPI/Starlette.
Example Attack/Impact: Attackers can bypass authentication logic by injecting credentials into proxy headers that are misinterpreted by the app.

Description: HTTP Request Smuggling in Starlette's header parsing.
Example Attack/Impact: A 'Transfer-Encoding: chunked' header sent along with 'Content-Length' can allow an attacker to smuggle a second request inside the first.

Description: Path traversal vulnerability in FastAPI's StaticFiles.
Example Attack/Impact: Requesting '/static/../../etc/passwd' might allow reading sensitive system files if not properly jailed.

Description: Resource Exhaustion (DoS) in multipart form data parsing.
Example Attack/Impact: Sending a large number of small parts in a multipart/form-data request to exhaust memory/CPU.

Description: Improper handling of session cookies leading to fixation/leakage.
Example Attack/Impact: An attacker sets a user's session ID before they log in, allowing the attacker to hijack the session after authentication.

Description: Incorrect validation of input types in Pydantic models.
Example Attack/Impact: Sending data types that the validator doesn't expect (e.g., extremely deep objects) to trigger crashes or unexpected logic.

Description: HTTP Request Smuggling in Hyper (Axum's engine) via header mismatch.
Example Attack/Impact: Sending conflicting Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding headers to confuse the proxy/server boundary.

Description: DoS in Hyper via malformed HTTP/2 requests.
Example Attack/Impact: Sending a flood of HTTP/2 HEADERS frames without closing the stream, causing 100% CPU usage.

Description: Request Smuggling in Hyper via incorrect whitespace handling.
Example Attack/Impact: Using leading/trailing whitespace in headers (e.g., 'Content-Length : 10') to bypass security filters.

Description: Host Name Poisoning in Hyper due to missing Host header validation.
Example Attack/Impact: Spoofing the Host header to trick the application into generating links to an attacker-controlled site.

Description: Command Injection via malformed arguments in Rust (Windows).
Example Attack/Impact: Executing 'cmd.exe /c "batchfile.bat & calc.exe"' where inputs weren't properly escaped for the shell.

Description: Memory safety issue in h2 crate (Axum/Hyper).
Example Attack/Impact: Sending a specific sequence of HTTP/2 frames that triggers an out-of-bounds access or crash.

Description: Spring4Shell: RCE via Class Injection in Data Binding.
Example Attack/Impact: Submitting a POST request with parameters like 'class.module.classLoader.resources.context.parent...' to create a web shell.

Description: Security bypass via specially crafted URL in Spring.
Example Attack/Impact: Using a double slash or encoded characters (e.g., '/admin//dashboard') to bypass an antPathMatcher check.

Description: RCE in Spring Messaging via SpEL injection.
Example Attack/Impact: Sending a STOMP message with a 'selector' header containing SpEL like 'T(java.lang.Runtime).getRuntime().exec("calc")'.

Description: RCE in Spring Cloud Function via routing-expression header.
Example Attack/Impact: Providing a malicious SpEL expression in the 'spring.cloud.function.routing-expression' header to execute code.

Description: DoS in Spring Framework via specific HTTP request handling.
Example Attack/Impact: Sending a crafted request that causes an infinite loop or excessive resource consumption in the framework.

Description: Expression injection leading to DoS/leakage in Spring.
Example Attack/Impact: Injecting SpEL expressions into application inputs that are subsequently evaluated by the framework.

Description: Off-by-one error in Nginx DNS resolver (RCE).
Example Attack/Impact: Responding to a DNS query from Nginx with a crafted packet that overflows a buffer when parsed.

Description: HTTP/2 'Data Drip' DoS in Nginx.
Example Attack/Impact: Requesting a large file and setting the window size to 1 byte, forcing the server to keep the connection open and consume memory.

Description: HTTP/2 'Resource Loop' (Ping-Pong) DoS in Nginx.
Example Attack/Impact: Sending a flood of SETTINGS frames that require an ACK, causing the server to enter a CPU-intensive loop.

Description: Stack-based buffer overflow in Nginx chunked encoding.
Example Attack/Impact: Sending a chunked request with a massive chunk size to overflow the internal buffer and execute shellcode.

Description: Memory corruption in Nginx mp4 module.
Example Attack/Impact: Uploading a malformed .mp4 file that, when processed by Nginx, causes a crash or code execution.

Description: Memory corruption in Nginx mp4 module (variant).
Example Attack/Impact: Similar to 41741, leveraging specific atom parsing in MP4 files to corrupt worker process memory.

Description: Path Traversal and RCE in Apache HTTP Server.
Example Attack/Impact: Requesting '/cgi-bin/.%2e/.%2e/.%2e/.%2e/etc/passwd' to read files or execute binaries.

Description: Incomplete fix for Apache Path Traversal (double encoding).
Example Attack/Impact: Using double-encoded path separators like '%%32%65%%32%65/' to bypass the initial fix for CVE-2021-41773.

Description: HTTP Request Smuggling in Apache (large body limits).
Example Attack/Impact: Sending a request with a body larger than the configured limit, which Apache misinterprets, allowing a smuggled request.

Description: Heap-based buffer overflow in mod_sed for Apache.
Example Attack/Impact: Sending a very large input to a resource handled by mod_sed to trigger a buffer overflow.

Description: Local Privilege Escalation in Apache parent process.
Example Attack/Impact: A script running in a worker process overwrites a scoreboard entry to execute code as the root parent process.

Description: Buffer overflow in mod_lua multipart parser.
Example Attack/Impact: Sending a multipart form request with a crafted boundary string to execute code via mod_lua.
